study type: Target trial emulation using g-computation on a retrospective cohort
cohort: The study included commercially insured, midwifery-eligible, low-risk pregnant individuals in the U.S. between 2004 and 2015, identified from an insurance claims data source.
finding: Increasing midwifery-led prenatal care reduced the prevalence of caesarean deliveries and maternal infections, while slightly increasing the prevalence of primary and secondary postpartum haemorrhage.
mod_finding: An increase in midwifery-led care led to a reduction in the prevalence of caesarean deliveries.
